output.root_problem: Dispute tickets doubled from ~600/month (Jun–Jul) to 1180–1260 (Aug–Sep) (E-01), and most disputed bills are ACTUAL-read, not estimated (E-04). Best-supported premise: bills built from actual reads (likely AMI reads via MDMS export and billing import validation) became wrong from August, because a read-delivery or validation defect lets bad or mis-mapped reads through; this is falsifiable via DA-MDMS, DA-RULES and DA-BILL.
output.requested_solution: Requester asks for an AI agent that auto-answers billing dispute tickets and fixes the cause of wrong bills. This is treated as a hypothesis, not the problem. Proposed instead: root-cause analysis of the actual-read path, with any bill or dispatch changes left to human-gated actions.
symptoms: Dispute tickets rose from 610/590 (Jun/Jul) to 1180/1260 (Aug/Sep) (E-01)
Disputed bills: 1785 ACTUAL vs 1240 ESTIMATED (E-04)
Route completion 0.88 vs 0.95 target, 9,200 manual-read accounts (E-03)
causal_chain: Read collection (AMI or manual) feeds MDMS validation and billing import via H-MDMS-BILL / H-FIELD-BILL; delivery and semantic validity are unverified.
From about August, a defect in the read path (candidate: AMI read delivery/mapping or a billing import validation rule change) lets incorrect actual reads reach billing (premise, not yet evidenced).
Bills issued from those reads are wrong, and a smaller share is estimated because of late routes (E-03, E-04).
Customers dispute the bills, so dispute tickets double (E-01).

assumptions.statement: The wrong actual-read bills arise in the AMI/MDMS-to-billing path rather than in manual reads that are labelled ACTUAL. This rests on the 1785 ACTUAL disputes and the absence of a tariff change.
The disputed-bill counts in E-04 cover a period comparable to the Aug–Sep ticket surge. The window of E-04 is not stated.
Field understaffing adds some estimated-bill disputes but does not explain the doubling. This rests on the fact that ACTUAL disputes outnumber ESTIMATED ones.
